species: rat (Sprague-Dawley); mouse (APP/PS1 double transgenic; C57BL/6 wild type)
readout_other: CA1/CA3 LFP, spike sorting and spike-field coherence; Y-maze spontaneous alternation; novel object location
direction_notes: Acute: peak-phase and random-phase stimulation raised slow gamma power and cross-frequency coupling; peak-phase also raised CA3-CA1 coherence. After 14 days, behaviour was unchanged in normal rats but improved in APP/PS1 mice with peak-phase stimulation, with increased CA1 power and CA3-CA1 coherence.

exposures.label: Phase-locked closed-loop ultrasound to CA3 (peak, trough, random phase)

timing.protocol_description: Pulses triggered on detection of a target phase of CA3 slow gamma (30-45 Hz): peak, trough or random phase. Acute experiment: 1, 2, 3 or 4 stimuli per second or all detected events. Chronic (rats and APP/PS1 mice): within each 1 s detection window one 10 ms pulse is triggered, 1 s interval between windows, 15 min per day for two weeks. Acoustic parameters are shown only in a figure.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirty-two SD rats were randomly divided into peak stimulation, trough stimulation, random stimulation, and sham stimulation groups (N=8 per group).
